title: How Hubert Thieblot grew Curse from a WoW add-on site into an MMOG portal (2007 interview)
summary: A 2007 Escapist interview where Thieblot explains how Curse began as a personal tool for his guild and grew to 3.5M monthly uniques. He covers solving his own problem, listening to user feedback, going broad as a portal versus narrow databases, and diversifying beyond one game.

principles.text: Build the product to solve your own problem first; it can grow into a real business.
principles.quote: I did it largely for myself and my fellow guild members to make it easier to acquire WoW add-ons.

principles.text: Spot a disorganized, painful workflow in a hot new ecosystem and organize it.
principles.quote: Early in that game, I realized that finding and downloading add-ons was an extremely difficult and disorganized undertaking – so Curse-Gaming was born

principles.text: Respond to user feedback fast; small quick fixes show commitment to the user experience.
principles.quote: So, within a day, we cranked out a great-looking dark color scheme, which many of our users have adopted.

principles.text: Differentiate by being the single centralized destination rather than a point solution addressing one need.
principles.quote: Our goal is to provide a single, centralized location for MMOG gamers to turn to, regardless of what they need.

principles.text: Don't depend on one platform's success; expand to new games and markets and build developer relationships.
principles.quote: We’re doing so in various ways, including actively fostering relationships with developers, in order to expand our support for existing and upcoming titles.

principles.text: Surround a young founding team with experienced operators from your industry.
principles.quote: we’ve actively surrounded the founding team with successful professionals who have experience in the videogame industry.
